newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay to apply for 3 pct fare rise.
newsitem.headline: Cathay to apply for 3 pct fare rise.

text.p: Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Thursday it will soon apply to the Civil Aviation Department (CAD) to raise air ticket prices by three percent to compensate for higher fuel costs.
"We are in the process of preparing application documents and hope to hand in an application to the CAD in the next few days," said Kwan Chuk-fai, manager of corporate communications.
The airline hoped the price rise could be implemented as soon as possible, depending on when the CAD approved it.
The three percent rise on published fares could only partly compensate for the increase in fuel prices over the past 12 months, Kwan said.
He said fuel prices, which accounted for about 15 percent of Cathay's operating costs, rose at least 30 percent in the last year.
Cathay's price rise decision comes after the International Air Transport Association (IATA) proposed to raise air ticket prices by three percent in response to a hefty rise in fuel prices.
